clue.text: Start of herbaceous border that runs around garden

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the thing that runs around a garden

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: A gardener describes the flowerbed that edges a whole garden, starting with herbaceous planting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long description of a herbaceous border; split it after 'border' and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is the line of shrubs planted to enclose a garden, so it is the boundary running round it.

clue.text: Under pressure, ran over nincompoop

indicators.note: one word is laid over the other, covering it on both sides

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so ran is hared

explanation.surface: Someone flustered and stressed has run down a fool, perhaps in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran over' looks like a single phrase about an accident, but ran is the outer word and over tells you it wraps round the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassed means hassled and stressed, which is what being under pressure feels like.

clue.text: Having a ball, like ladies, one over the eight

definitions.note: a phrase describing the activity, as the participle does
definitions.meaning: first meaning: what people are doing at a ball, enjoying themselves on the floor

definitions.text: like ladies, one over the eight
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase matching the participle used as an adjective
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in the carol the gift for day nine, one more than eight, is ladies doing this

explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being drunk, steering you to merry partygoers; here it simply means nine, as in nine ladies of the Twelve Days of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing is both the activity at a ball and the description of the nine ladies in the Christmas carol.

clue.text: Composed poems in place of classics course?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by description

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone wrote poems instead of attending a course on Greek and Latin literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Classics here are not Latin and Greek but the five Classic horse races of English flat racing; Epsom Downs racecourse hosts two of them, the Derby and the Oaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is the racecourse where the Classic races called the Derby and the Oaks are run.

clue.text: Poet as deliverer of annual Christmas message

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Alexander ..., the eighteenth-century English poet
second meaning: the head of the Catholic Church, who gives the Urbi et Orbi blessing each Christmas Day

explanation.walkthrough: The annual Christmas message suggests the British monarch's broadcast, but the other figure giving one every year is the leader of the Catholic Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope wrote The Rape of the Lock, and the pontiff addresses the world each Christmas from St Peter's.

clue.text: Flier received initially at Christmas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a game bird, something that flies

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for a noun; fair because it describes the gift itself, the first one received
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the gift on the first day in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: A flier sounds like a printed leaflet; here it is a bird, and initially means on the first of the twelve days.
explanation.definitionFit: In the carol, my true love's gift on the first day is a game bird sitting in a pear tree.

clue.text: Piano put in middle of jetty for musician

indicators.note: placing something in the middle of a word means it sits inside it

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano is wheeled out onto a pier so a musician can play there.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is a musician who plays the bagpipes or a pipe, like the eleven in the carol.

clue.text: Finishes off list — whatever you receive is genuine

indicators.note: the finish of each word is its last letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: closing letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Whatever you find under the tree is real, says someone ticking off a Christmas list.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine are synonyms, both meaning real or authentic.

clue.text: Unruly carnival location, from our perspective

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosts the most famous carnival

explanation.surface: From where we stand, the carnival city looks rather wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous means wild and disorderly, the same sense as unruly behaviour that is hard to control.

clue.text: 5 and his fellow players counted in cricket side

definitions.note: the count of the musicians, a number
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the answer to 5 is a piper, and the carol has this many of them piping
second meaning: a cricket team has this many players

explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'cricket side' make it sound like one sporting team, but the first players are musicians from the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's day-eleven gift is that number of pipers, and a cricket team fields the same number of players.

clue.text: Bands, five of which are featured in Christmas song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: circular bands, as worn on fingers

definitions.text: five of which are featured in Christmas song
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the five gold ones given on the fifth day of the carol

explanation.walkthrough: Bands suggests musical groups playing a Christmas song, but they are circles of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings are circular bands of metal, and five gold ones are the famous fifth-day gift in the carol.

clue.text: Transported as gifts are, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound rather than its spelling

explanation.surface: Presents are carried off, and wrapped too, if your ears are to be believed.
explanation.walkthrough: Transported here means enchanted, carried away with delight, not shipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly absorbed or enraptured, and transported is used in the same sense of carried away by emotion.

clue.text: Cause of world revolution? It's partly reversed

indicators.note: something reversed runs the other way, so the letters are read right to left
only part of a word is taken, a run of letters sitting inside it

parts.note: letters two to five of the word revolution

explanation.surface: Asked what makes the whole world turn, the answer is that it is only half backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points back at its own word revolution: part of it, turned round, gives the answer. 'Love makes the world go round' is the saying behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says love makes the world go round, so it is the thing causing the world's turning.

clue.text: Number of days in present period

definitions.text: Number of days in present period

parts.words: Number of days in present period
parts.note: surface reading: how many days there are in the current period of time; setter's reading: the length of the festive gift-giving season in the carol

explanation.walkthrough: Present looks like 'current'; it means gift, and the present period is the Christmas stretch from Christmas Day to Epiphany.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol counts gifts over the Twelve Days of Christmas, from 25 December to 5 January.

clue.text: Show anger about women's swan, one of seven

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to simmer is to seethe quietly with anger
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: An angry outburst about a women's swan, which is one of a group of seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol gives seven swans a-swimming, so one of them is described by what it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the carol's seven swans is swimming, so a swan among them is a swimmer, one who swims.

clue.text: We're wrong to include rubbish put down, in other words

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside
letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: We're mistaken to include rubbish in what we wrote down, someone admits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' alone could mean insulted; 'in other words' turns it into writing something out again differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewrite is to set down a text again in new wording, which is what putting it down in other words means.

clue.text: Number of those working in dairy — or having a row?

definitions.text: Number of those working in dairy
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the count of maids a-milking in the carol

definitions.note: describes a rowing crew, a noun, by what it is doing
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rowing crew of this many oarsmen

explanation.walkthrough: Having a row suggests an argument among the dairy staff; it is a boat race. An eight is a rowing boat with eight oars.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol has eight maids a-milking, and in rowing an eight is a crew of eight oarsmen.

clue.text: Queen's consort?

parts.note: surface reading: the husband of a monarch; setter's reading: a queen is also a female cat, so her mate is a male cat

explanation.walkthrough: A queen is the breeding term for a female cat; the male partner has a familiar name.
explanation.definitionFit: Female cats are called queens and male cats toms, so the queen's mate is the male cat.

clue.text: Protest by left is hard to refute completely

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A political point: a protest organised by the left is hard to argue against.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish an argument is to destroy it utterly, so refuting it completely is the figurative sense.

clue.text: Part of Christmas decoration that depends on host

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sprig hung up at Christmas for kissing under

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a plant that lives on another
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a parasitic plant that grows on a host tree

explanation.walkthrough: Host suggests whoever throws the Christmas party; it is the tree the plant feeds on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is hung at Christmas and is a parasite that draws water and nutrients from a host tree such as apple.

clue.text: With arms raised, cape gives comfortable feeling

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: Someone raises their arms and their cloak gives them a cosy feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape looks like a garment but is a headland; NESS appears in English place names such as Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Snugness is the state of being cosy and warm, so it is a comfortable feeling.

clue.text: Players having their day, though not in first eleven

definitions.text: Players having their day, though not in first eleven

parts.words: Players having their day, though not in first eleven
parts.note: surface reading: sportsmen who get their chance even though they are not in the first team; setter's reading: the musicians who are the carol's gift on day twelve, after the first eleven days

explanation.walkthrough: 'First eleven' is a school or club's top cricket or football team; here it means the first eleven days of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's last gift, on the twelfth day, is twelve players beating drums.

clue.text: Predate unusually excessive formality

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an odd order

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic complaint that excessive formality goes back further than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is bureaucratic procedure, named after the ribbon that once tied official documents.

clue.text: Strange sense in which most citizens are German

definitions.text: in which most citizens are German
definitions.note: describes a place, standing for the city

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd feeling that most of the citizens around are German.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a large industrial city in the Ruhr, so most people living there are German.

clue.text: Taking a risk, we poorly selected gear for travelling on snow

indicators.note: something poorly selected is badly sorted, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: We chose badly, a gamble on clothing for a winter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiwear is the clothing designed for skiing, which is travelling over snow.

clue.text: Pages penned by writer in verse for sweetheart

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: pp is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: A poet fills pages with lines for his beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: Penned looks like 'written', which suits a poet; here it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is an affectionate British term for a dear or darling, used much like sweetheart.

clue.text: Veteran that's discarded in reshuffle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an experienced person

definitions.note: a relative phrase standing for a noun; fair because it describes the thing itself, the previous deal of cards
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the previous set of cards dealt, thrown back when the pack is shuffled

explanation.walkthrough: Reshuffle suggests a cabinet change in which a veteran minister is dropped; read literally it is a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is an expert with long experience, and literally the previous deal of cards before the next shuffle.

clue.text: As result of song for couple, love follows

parts.note: a duet is sung by two
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Because of a love song for two, romance follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Due to means because of, so it introduces the result of a cause.

clue.text: Like ten nobles below, going into spring

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, like the participle
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ten lords of the carol, the answer to 34 below, are doing this

definitions.note: a participle phrase, as the answer is
definitions.meaning: second meaning: launching into a jump

explanation.walkthrough: Spring suggests the season; here it is a jump. 'Below' points at 34 Across, the lords a-leaping of the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaping means jumping, which is going into a spring, and the carol's ten lords are a-leaping.

clue.text: Christmas visitor appearing in strange light

indicators.note: letters appearing in a phrase are found inside it, across the word gap

explanation.surface: A Christmas visitor shows up in an eerie glow, as in the Nativity story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' tempts you to rearrange 'light', but the answer simply sits across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Nativity story an angel visits the shepherds to announce the birth of Jesus.

clue.text: Silly repartee in home of 4 Down

indicators.note: something silly is nonsensical, so the letters are rearranged into sense

explanation.surface: Foolish banter going on in a partridge's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's first gift is a partridge in a pear tree, so that tree is where the bird lives.

clue.text: Some Christmas entertainment was elating

definitions.note: a past-tense verb phrase, as the answer is

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a portion of its letters, a run lying inside

explanation.surface: Part of the Christmas show was thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Sent here is the old slang sense of thrilled, as in 'that music really sends me'.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone is informal for to thrill or delight them, so sent means was elating.

clue.text: Half a dozen layers among seasonal gifts

definitions.text: Half a dozen layers among seasonal gifts

parts.words: Half a dozen layers among seasonal gifts
parts.note: surface reading: six hens, or six sheets of wrapping, under the Christmas tree; setter's reading: the six birds a-laying given on the sixth day of the carol

explanation.walkthrough: Layers could be strata or wrapping, but they are egg-laying birds from the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's sixth-day gift is six geese a-laying, birds that lay eggs.

clue.text: See 29
Major work that's sung after my 6 11 30

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large heavy book

definitions.note: refers to the words that come next in the song
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the answers to 6, 11 and 30 give 'true love sent'

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the cross-references to get the carol's line 'my true love sent to me'; the two words that follow join to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large weighty book, and the carol line 'my true love sent to me' ends with these two words.

clue.text: House that's HQ for sport in London

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the upper chamber of the UK Parliament
second meaning: ..., the London ground that is the home of cricket

explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the UK Parliament's upper chamber; Lord's Cricket Ground in north London is called the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords names both the upper house of Parliament and the famous London cricket ground headquarters of the MCC.
